title: Paying Attention: Overnight Returns and the Hidden Cost of Buying at the Open
one_line: High-attention stocks rise overnight (+13 bp) and fall during the day (−13 bp) because retail buying at the open inflates opening prices; across all stocks opening prices sit ~8 bp above the prior closing midquote and fall during the first hour; the pattern tracks sentiment.

findings.statement: High-attention portfolio: overnight +13 bp, day −13 bp; hard-to-value stocks +43/−45 bp.
All stocks: overnight ≈ +10 bp, day ≈ −7 bp; open ≈ 8 bp above prior close midquote; first-hour decline.
Correlates with Baker-Wurgler sentiment (+0.30 overnight, −0.33 day).

why.pattern: Retail attention-driven buying at the open.

reported_results.headline: High-attention stocks rise overnight (+13 bp) and fall during the day (−13 bp) because retail buying at the open inflates opening prices; across all stocks opening prices sit ~8 bp above the prior closing midquote and fall during the first hour; the pattern tracks sentiment.

tradable_edge: Stock-level, but supports the first-hour fade idea already in overnight_reversal_first_hour_es / open_imbalance_fade_es (after a gap up). No new spec.
data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 5, 2026-11-10), not by the weekly pipeline.
